title: Show endpoint returns the domain entity instead of the API DTO
observable: GET /api/v1/users/{id} (valid token, existing user) returns 200 with data {"ID":"1","Name":"Ann"} (capitalised keys) instead of {"id":"1","name":"Ann"}. List and update responses are unaffected.

title: Bearer tokens without an exp claim are accepted
observable: GET /api/v1/users with an HS256 token signed with JWT_SECRET, correct iss and aud, but no exp claim returns 200 with the user list instead of 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} with WWW-Authenticate containing error="invalid_token".

title: Update handler maps an oversized body to 400 instead of 413
observable: PUT /api/v1/users/{id} with a valid token, Content-Type application/json and a ~2 MiB JSON body (e.g. {"name":"a","pad":"<2 MiB of x>"}) returns 400 {"error":"Failed to read request body"} instead of 413 {"error":"Request body too large"}. POST /api/v1/users with the same body still returns 413.

title: Create treats an empty request body as an empty object
observable: POST /api/v1/users with a valid token, Content-Type application/json and an empty body returns 422 {"message":"name is required","error":"Validation failed"} instead of 400 {"error":"Failed to read request body"}. PUT with an empty body still returns 400.

title: Content-Type check compares the raw header, rejecting media-type parameters
observable: POST /api/v1/users (valid token) with Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 and body {"name":"Ann"} returns 415 {"error":"Content-Type must be application/json"} instead of 201; no row is inserted. Same for POST /login with that header (415 instead of 200/401).

title: Content-Type check no longer applies to PUT
observable: PUT /api/v1/users/{id} (valid token) with Content-Type: text/plain and body {"name":"Bob"} returns 200 {"message":"User updated successfully",...} and the users row is renamed to Bob, instead of 415 with the row unchanged. POST with text/plain still returns 415.

title: Body size cap is 1,000,000 bytes instead of 1 MiB
observable: POST /api/v1/users (valid token, application/json) with a well-formed body of about 1,030,000 bytes (e.g. {"name":"Ann","pad":"<1,030,000 x>"}) returns 413 {"error":"Request body too large"} instead of 201; no row is inserted. Bodies over 1,048,576 bytes return 413 in both versions.

title: Vary: Origin is only sent for allowed cross-origin requests
observable: Any request without an Origin header (e.g. GET /api/v1/users with a valid token, or an unauthenticated one getting 401, or POST /login) lacks the Vary: Origin response header, which the original always sends on /api/* and /login.

title: Security headers applied only to the application routes
observable: GET /healthz, GET /readyz and POST /login (any status, e.g. 405 for GET /login) no longer carry X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy or Content-Security-Policy. Responses under /api/v1/users still have them.

title: Empty list page serialises data as [] instead of null
observable: GET /api/v1/users on an empty table, or with ?cursor= pointing past the last row (e.g. the next_cursor of the second-to-last page followed to the end), returns {"message":"Fetched users successfully","data":[]} instead of {"message":"Fetched users successfully","data":null}.

title: Login rate limiter off by one: throttles on the limit-th attempt
observable: Five POST /login attempts for username admin with a wrong password within a minute: the original answers 401 to all five and 429 (with Retry-After) to the sixth; the mutant answers 429 {"error":"too many login attempts"} to the fifth.

title: User ids parsed as 64-bit and truncated to int32
observable: With user id 1 present, GET /api/v1/users/4294967297 returns 200 with user 1 instead of 404 {"error":"Not found"}; DELETE /api/v1/users/4294967297 deletes row id 1 from the users table; PUT renames it. GET /api/v1/users?cursor=<base64url of 4294967296> returns the first page instead of 400.

title: Update WHERE clause matches every row with id >= target
observable: With users 1, 2, 3 present, PUT /api/v1/users/2 {"name":"Zed"} returns 200 as usual, but in the users table rows 2 AND 3 now have name Zed (original: only row 2). With a single row, or updating the highest id, nothing differs.

title: Delete of a non-existent user reports success
observable: DELETE /api/v1/users/999999 (no such row), or deleting the same id twice, returns 200 {"message":"deleted user with ID of 999999 successfully"} instead of 404 {"error":"Not found"}. Non-numeric/out-of-range ids still return 404.

title: Update validates the name only after writing it
observable: PUT /api/v1/users/{id} {"name":""} on an existing user returns 422 as before, but the users row's name is now '' (original: unchanged). PUT with a 101-character name returns 500 {"error":"Database operation failure"} instead of 422; PUT {"name":""} on a missing id returns 404 instead of 422.

title: Update only checks for an empty name, skipping length and character rules
observable: PUT /api/v1/users/{id} {"name":"a\u0007b"} or {"name":"a\tb"} returns 200 and stores the control character in the users table instead of 422 {"error":"Validation failed","message":"name contains invalid characters"}; PUT with a 101-character name returns 500 {"error":"Database operation failure"} instead of 422. POST still validates fully.

title: Name length limit counts bytes instead of characters
observable: POST /api/v1/users {"name":"<60 x U+00E9 'e-acute'>"} (60 characters, 120 UTF-8 bytes) returns 422 {"message":"name is too long","error":"Validation failed"} instead of 201; same for PUT. ASCII names behave as before.

title: next_cursor emitted when the page is exactly full with no more rows
observable: With exactly 3 users, GET /api/v1/users?limit=3 returns all 3 plus a next_cursor field (original: no next_cursor); following that cursor returns {"data":null} with no cursor. Pages that are not exactly full at the end of the table are unaffected.

title: next_cursor built from the first item of the page instead of the last
observable: With 5 users and limit=2: GET /api/v1/users?limit=2 returns ids 1,2; following next_cursor returns ids 2,3 (overlapping) instead of 3,4. Walking all pages repeats rows. With limit=1 the behaviour is identical.

title: Negative limit is not replaced by the default page size
observable: With 5+ users, GET /api/v1/users?limit=-1 returns a single user plus next_cursor instead of up to 20 users (default page size) with no cursor. ?limit=0 and missing limit still use the default.

title: Malformed (non-base64) cursor surfaces as a 500
observable: GET /api/v1/users?cursor=!!! (valid token) returns 500 {"error":"Database operation failure"} instead of 400 {"error":"Invalid pagination cursor"}. A well-formed base64 cursor with a non-numeric or out-of-range payload still returns 400.

title: Token issuer is no longer checked
observable: GET /api/v1/users with an HS256 token signed with JWT_SECRET, valid exp, aud users-api-postgres but iss "another-service" (or no iss at all) returns 200 with the list instead of 401 {"error":"unauthorized"}.

title: Bearer scheme compared case-sensitively
observable: GET /api/v1/users with Authorization: bearer <valid token> (lower-case scheme) returns 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm=... instead of 200. "Bearer <token>" still works.

title: Invalid-token 401 omits error="invalid_token" from WWW-Authenticate
observable: GET /api/v1/users with Authorization: Bearer garbage (or an expired/wrong-signature token) returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="users-api-postgres" instead of Bearer realm="users-api-postgres", error="invalid_token". A request with no Authorization header is unchanged.

title: Successful login no longer resets the per-username attempt counter
observable: Six POST /login requests with the correct admin credentials within one minute: the original returns 200 with a token every time; the mutant returns 429 {"error":"too many login attempts"} with Retry-After on the sixth.
